citations.narrative:
Supplies of food are not being stored in a manner that protects the supplies from spoilage, contamination and vermin.
The fruit is stored in plastic bins and when the bins were pulled open, there was an abundance of fruit flies that swarmed
up and around the produce and multiple items showed signs of being spoiled. These items are not refrigerated and
therefore spoil quickly in the main facility.
There were strawberries, tomatoes and other produce sitting in bins with water in the kitchen sink rinsed off, but there was
also cleaning detergent and an all-purpose cleaner right next to the sink which could potentially contaminate the fruit if it
fall into the sink. Cleaning agents such as these must not be stored in food storage and preparation areas for the safety of
the animals.
Supplies of food and bedding must be stored in a manner that protects the supplies from spoilage, contamination, and
vermin infestation. Food requiring refrigeration must be stored accordingly, and all food must be stored in a manner that
prevents contamination and deterioration of its nutritive value. Substances that are toxic to the nonhuman primates but
that are required for normal husbandry practices must not be stored in food storage and preparation areas, but may be
stored in cabinets in the animal areas.
Correct By: Sept 5, 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Enclosures are not being spot cleaned daily. Several of the enclosures have a build up of feces that need to be removed.
Feces and food waste need to be removed from inside each indoor primary enclosure daily to reduce an accumulation of
waste and to reduce odors and pest issues.
The fire hoses that are hung in several of the enclosures has a thick layer of brownish build up covering a majority of the
hose that the animals use in the enclosure.
Failure to clean as often as necessary can lead to the buildup of secretion, feces, and debris which may attract insects or
vermin, and increase the risk of disease transmission.
Due to the scent-marking nature of this species, items in the enclosure must be kept clean or replaced when worn or
soiled for the health of the animals. and to keep them from becoming soiled.
Correct by: Sept 5, 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Housekeeping for the facility needs to be addressed. The facility has multiple empty un occupied enclosures that have not
been cleaned and sanitized and are stored next to enclosures housing animals.
One of the dirty enclosures has old toys, furniture, shavings and food bowls that have not been cleaned since the
previous animal moved out of the enclosure several weeks ago. Two other empty enclosures also have furniture, toys and
shavings that have not been removed and cleaned despite the enclosures being empty for more than a week.
Along the window at the front of the building, there is a TV, excess cardboard and a planter that need to be moved to
reduce living areas for mice. The metal cage and bottom that is empty next to these items had rodent droppings in the
metal tray and there is old shavings on the floor that need to be removed to keep the area clean.
There is a box fan not being utilized, some cardboard and excess materials along the wall on the driveway side of the
facility. These unused items just clutter the area and do not keep the area clean and in good repair.
The ceiling throughout the facility has cobwebs that need to be removed.
Buildings must be kept clean and in good repair in order to protect the nonhuman primates from injury, to facilitate the
husbandry practices required in this subpart, and to reduce or eliminate breeding and living areas for rodents, pests, and
vermin. Premises must be kept free of accumulations of trash, junk, waste, and discarded matter.
Correct by: Sept 15, 2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
The facility does not have an effective program for the control of flies and mice throughout the building. There were mice
droppings throughout the facility and along the window ledges and in old unused enclosures that are being stored next to
occupied enclosures. There is also an abundance of fruit flies all around the diet prep room and among the produce bins.
An effective program for control of insects, external parasites affecting nonhuman primates, and birds and mammals that
are pests, must be established and maintained so as to promote the health and well-being of the animals and reduce
contamination by pests in animal areas.
Correct by: Sept 20, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
